technical_and_design_decisions: The increment targets the Spring Integration project (despite the generic Spring Framework background text) based on the module names (Mail, SFTP, aggregator, bridge, http-client, reactor-*).
Acceptance tests will be implemented using JUnit 5 and Spring's testing support (Spring Boot Test, @SpringBootTest) consistent with modern Spring projects.

Testcontainers will be used to provide real, isolated, embedded instances of external dependencies (SFTP server, SMTP/Mail server, HTTP server, Syslog receiver) so that tests validate real end-to-end behavior rather than mocked interactions.

Tests will live in a dedicated acceptance test source set/source root (e.g., src/test/java with the 'acceptance' classifier or a separate Maven/Gradle source set) so they are clearly distinct from unit tests.
A shared acceptance-test support module/helper class will be created to reduce duplication across the eight modules (common context loading, polling utilities, channel interceptors).

CI build integration will use the existing project build tool (Maven or Gradle) with a dedicated profile/task ('acceptanceTest') wired into the CI pipeline so the tests run on every CI build as the user stories require.

Each module's acceptance test suite will cover the public API entry points and main happy-path, error-path, and configuration scenarios (e.g., for aggregator: correlation strategy, release strategy, timeout; for SFTP: inbound polling, file transfer, key-based auth).
Tests will be written to be deterministic and idempotent so they can be safely re-run on every CI build.

Per-module effort is scaled by complexity: SFTP and PMML are highest (real external protocol/model evaluation), aggregator and http-client are medium (state machines / real HTTP), bridge and reactor-* are lower (simpler channel/reactive interactions).
assumptions: The developer is a single experienced Java/Spring developer working 8 productive work-hours per day.
The project already has a working CI build (Maven or Gradle) and unit test infrastructure; effort covers only adding acceptance tests and wiring them into the existing CI pipeline.
The eight source/processor modules already exist in production-ready form; this increment does not include implementing or fixing module functionality, only adding test coverage.
External test dependencies (e.g., Docker for Testcontainers) are available in the CI environment; otherwise 4-6 additional hours may be needed for environment provisioning.
Acceptance tests are end-to-end behavioral tests validating real functionality (not just compile-time or smoke tests).
Documentation effort is limited to in-code Javadoc/comments and a short README addition; no separate user-facing documentation is required.
No code review iteration delays are included beyond a single internal review pass; external review cycles are out of scope.
1 work-hour is used as the unit of effort (excludes meetings beyond a single planning touch-point and excludes waiting time for CI runs).
Effort for fixing any defects discovered in the modules themselves while writing the tests is bounded to a small allocation within each module's estimate; large refactors are out of scope.
Reactor-based modules (reactor-ip, reactor-syslog) use Project Reactor; the developer is assumed to be proficient with reactive streams testing (StepVerifier, etc.).

activities.activity_name: Project analysis and acceptance test strategy
activities.activity_description: Review each of the eight modules' public APIs, existing tests, and documentation; define the acceptance test scope, conventions, naming, and shared utilities to be used across all eight modules.

activities.activity_name: Acceptance test framework and shared infrastructure setup
activities.activity_description: Set up the acceptance test source set, JUnit 5 configuration, Spring Test support, Testcontainers base classes, and shared helper utilities (e.g., embedded server lifecycle, message capturing, channel verification).

Configure the Maven/Gradle build to expose a dedicated acceptance-test task wired into the existing CI configuration, add Surefire/Failsafe (or equivalent) reporting, and verify tests run as part of every CI build.
Implement acceptance tests for the Mail source: inbound mail reception via embedded SMTP server (Testcontainers), IMAP/POP3 polling, message conversion, and error scenarios.
Implement acceptance tests for the reactor-ip source: reactive UDP/TCP-based message ingress, backpressure behavior, and StepVerifier-based verification of emitted messages.
Implement acceptance tests for the reactor-syslog source: syslog message parsing (RFC 3164/5424), reactive reception over UDP/TCP, and malformed-message handling.

Implement acceptance tests for the SFTP source: embedded SFTP server (Testcontainers with atmoz/sftp or similar), key-based/password auth, file listing, file transfer, filtering, post-processing, and remote-directory scenarios.
Implement acceptance tests for the aggregator processor: correlation strategies, release strategies (size, timeout, sequence-header), expiration, force-complete, and group-timeout scenarios.
Implement acceptance tests for the analytic-pMML processor: loading PMML models, evaluating sample inputs, verifying model output mapping, and handling unsupported/edge-case inputs.
